taxonomic_note: Reviewed accepted species treatment elevated from P. foetida var. lanuginosa in 2023; historical P. foetida sensu lato observations must not be silently mapped to this taxon.
look_here_first: Introduced scarletfruit passionflower comparison (not confirmed native to your target counties). Look first for an actual RIPE FRUIT: usually smooth and vivid red in the documented P. lanuginosa concept, versus greenish/yellow-green fruit in the locally reviewed P. foetida concept. Then inspect finely divided bract cage, hairy leaf and stem, and often more sharply pointed/angular leaf lobes. Older P. foetida var. lanuginosa specimens require taxonomic reconciliation; don't identify it by flower color or a fruit photo alone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Completed deep review cites Kew/POWO native range eastern Mexico to Guatemala; Texas observations treated as introduced. No native target-zone county evidence.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not count introduced Bexar/San Antonio observations as evidence of target-zone nativity; historical P. foetida var. lanuginosa records require concept reconciliation.

best_field_traits: Tendrilled climbing or scrambling passionflower with bracts enclosing flower/fruit
Leaves commonly darker and more angular or pointed-lobed than local P. foetida comparison
Flowers often pinkish; flower color alone insufficient
Fruit smooth and ripening red in the reviewed species concept
Verify bract structure, leaf shape, fruit surface and maturity together
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Contrast fruit surface/color and leaf-lobe shape against canonical P. foetida; do not identify only from pink flowers or a single photograph. Use a full flower/fruit-bract view and mature fruit close-up.

comparisons.key_distinctions: P. foetida in the local learner has rounded 3-lobed leaves, strong fetid odor, dense soft pubescence, a finely divided sticky-bracted cage, and green-to-yellow-green fruit in the reviewed Texas concept; P. lanuginosa tends toward more angular/pointed leaves and smooth red-ripe fruit. The P. ciliata name has also been applied to introduced lookalikes in the San Antonio area; verify the current taxon concept rather than assuming every nonnative foetida-like plant is P. lanuginosa.
